patch_description:
The current program uses extreme parameter sharing (single "theta" parameter) which achieves high parameter efficiency but sacrifices expressiveness and accuracy. The prior programs show that moderate parameter sharing with diverse gate types and strategic connectivity patterns yields better accuracy (0.90-0.92 test) while maintaining reasonable parameter counts (44-50 params).

The recommendation suggests alternating CZ-chain rewiring: dynamically cycle the dense CZ pattern across ansatz blocks to inject broader connectivity without adding gates. This builds on the rapid convergence of dense-CZ designs while improving expressiveness.

The new approach:
1. Restore moderate parameter sharing (separate parameters for different qubit groups and gate types) to improve expressiveness
2. Implement alternating CZ connectivity: even-indexed blocks use standard nearest-neighbor + cross-block CZ, odd-indexed blocks shift the pattern by one qubit (modulo 8)
3. Add parametrized two-qubit gates (CRY, CRZ) for controlled entanglement
4. Maintain efficient parameter count (~40-45 params) while improving accuracy and reducing the train-test gap
5. Use RX, RY, RZ rotations with strategic parameter sharing to balance expressiveness and efficiency

This design leverages the success of the prior programs while implementing the alternating connectivity recommendation to achieve better generalization and faster convergence.
